Every faction (Gangs.cs fields by name). Leave a field out to keep the built-in value; a new Id = a new faction. Name lists: a NameBank name ("IrishFirst") or a list. Districts: zone hashes as hex. Tiers: Label / MinRank / Seats, top first. Seed: Rank / Count / Models. Relations: other faction id -> -100..100 (either side may say it). Jobs: Title / Place with {t} = the town, Crew; JobTowns: where they happen.

Districts: Key, Name, X / Y (its middle), Hashes (the zone hashes the game gives for it, hex), Lore (faction id -> starting hold 0-100; a faction's encounter weight there = hold / 18). Towns: Name (the game's zone name), Doctor / Saloon [x, y, z] (either may be missing), CoreRadius (the busy part, m).

TURMOIL world events (Sandbox.cs): Weight = how often turmoil comes up next to the [World] weights (clash 20, life 60...), Kinds = each wildcard's weight (0 = never). Incident lines: {a} {b} = the two factions, {p} / {d} = the district.

Easy, mister. We're watching this road.
Keep your hands where I can see 'em and move along.
There's a war on. Don't make yourself part of it.
Nobody rides through here without us seeing. Go on.
Colm's watching this town now. Mind yourself.
Move along, friend - this is O'Driscoll business.
Lemoyne's ours. You just passing through?
Move along - and don't go telling no Yankees what you seen.
Halt. State your business - never mind, move along.
This town's under watch. Keep it peaceful.
Mr Bronte's men are minding the street. Be on your way.
Nothing to see here. Keep walking.
You'd do well to keep riding.
Ain't no business of yours what goes on here.
You lost? Best get lost further.
Go on through, friend. Nobody's shooting today.
That's far enough. Turn around - we know who you are.
Turn back. Your kind don't ride through here.
Not another step. Go back the way you came.
Sure. I could use the air.
Why not. Dutch won't miss me for a while.
Alright, Arthur. Don't get us killed.
Now you're talking! Me and you, Arthur - legends!
Yeah, alright. Somebody's gotta watch your back.
Fine. But I ain't cleaning nothing.
Thank God. One more pot of stew and I'd scream.
I'll keep up. Don't you worry.
An old man's company? Very well.
Why not. My bones could use the road.
Is there whiskey where we're going?
Sure, sugar. Let's raise some hell.
Well now, Black Lung wants company. Sure.
Fine, cowpoke. Try and keep up.
If you'll have me, Mister Morgan.
Alright, Arthur. Let's see what this country holds.
For you, son - I'll make the time.
I'll come... but I ain't doing no lifting.
Fine, fine. My lumbago and me.
Not now, Arthur. I've got plans to make.
Later, son. I need to think.
My lumbago, Arthur. You know how it is.
I'd love to... but I just sat down.
I got my own business, Morgan.
Somebody has to run this camp, Mister Morgan.
And who'll feed this lot? No, sir.
I have accounts to settle, Mister Morgan.
I got Jack to look after.
I got work to do here.
Tracks here. Deer, a day old.
Quiet out here. I like it.
You ever think about leaving all this?
You think Dutch's got a plan? A real one?
I read about this country in a book once.
Race you to the next ridge!
Reminds me of home, a little.
I'd play the guitar if I'd brought it.
Dutch will see us through. He always does.
Don't look at me like that.
Some days I think about runnin'.
Did I ever tell you about me da?
We should rob a train. A big one.
Ireland's got nothing on these hills. Well, maybe a bit.
I could eat a whole horse.
You think I'm stupid, don't you.
Army taught me one thing - keep your powder dry.
I can shoot as well as any of you.
Dutch and I rode roads like this, years ago.
Mind the man, not the gun.
You're a better man than you think, Arthur.
This land's ripe for the picking.
You and me, Morgan - we ain't so different.
The O'Driscolls'd skin me if they saw me.
I like horses better than people.
We just need a little more money.
Argh - I'm done, I'm done! I'll see you at camp!
They got me! I'm pullin' back!
I'll see you back at camp.
Looks like {0}'s got something for you. I'll head back.
That's {0} - gang business. I'll see you at camp.
{0}'s waiting on you. I'll get out of the way.
You go see {0}. I'll ride on back.
Sean, you owe me a drink.
I owe everyone a drink, Karen. That's the beauty of it.
And you love every word of it.
You keep up all right, Lenny.
Keep your eyes to yourself, Micah.
Something about you I don't trust.
Dutch trusts you, Micah. I don't.
Lucky I don't need your trust, amigo.
You think you're smarter'n me, Bell?
You should spend more time with your son, John.
I-I never meant no harm, Sean.
Not if I can help it, Lenny boy.
Gracias, Charles. You should sing with me sometime.
We always need a plan, Dutch. We need a good one.
Good to be out of that camp.
Arthur rides like he's got somewhere to be.
Funny, I was gonna say the same.
How far you reckon we're going?
Quiet out here. Too quiet, maybe.
You ever think about just... stopping? Somewhere like this?
Take your time, Arthur. I ain't in a hurry.
Don't see country like this back east.
We waitin' on something, or just waitin'?
Wake me when you're done brooding.
Horses could use the rest too.
Good to be out of the weather.
Keep an eye on that door.
Folks are lookin' at us, Arthur.
Don't touch nothing you can't pay for.
Smells like old coffee in here.
Buy a man a drink, Arthur?
That fella at the table's been cheating all night.
I'd sit in on a hand if I had any money.
Keep your voice down - half this room's wanted somewhere.

If I had a dollar for every time we stopped...

Pop always said sit when you can.
You can hear everything, if you listen.
I could play something, if I had my guitar.
Back home we'd be eating by now.
You think Dutch knows what he's doing?
Abigail'd have my hide if she saw me sittin' around.

When you're my age, every chair's a blessing.
Dutch used to be different, you know.
I ain't stupid, Arthur. I know what you're thinking.
You and me, cowpoke. We think alike.
Mr. Morgan... thank you. For bringing me.
Finally, a rest. My lumbago, Arthur.
I was a cowboy once, you know.
